evidence_status: adaptation benefit supported at the studied-sample level
scope: descriptive and sample-level inference for participants 3-9
supported_conclusion: Cumulative prior-session retraining improved balanced accuracy on average in this seven-participant sample, but the benefit was participant- and session-dependent.
important_tension: The participant-level Wilcoxon test and clustered bootstrap support a positive mean effect, while the two-sided participant sign test does not reach 0.05 with only seven participants.
not_supported: A universal benefit in every participant or session
A causal neural-adaptation or neuroplasticity conclusion
A claim that covariance drift identifies the physical source of change
Population-level generalization beyond the studied sample
recommended_claim: Across seven participants and 35 future-session comparisons, cumulative prior-session retraining increased mean balanced accuracy from 0.597 to 0.635. The participant-clustered 95% bootstrap interval for mean gain was approximately 0.017 to 0.053. Six of seven participants improved on average, but session-level losses occurred, so adaptation should be monitored and selectively applied rather than assumed beneficial.
recommended_next_measurement: Evaluate a policy that enables adaptation only when held-out or online monitoring predicts benefit, and collect electrode/contact-quality or impedance metadata to separate recording-interface drift from neural change.
